answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 but they are not the same

events.what_changed: Art. 6 used to guarantee migrants and their families equal access to the same protection and rights as nationals, including justice. It now adds 'de acuerdo con los derechos y obligaciones correspondientes a cada categoría migratoria', which ties equal access to migratory category. This touches the indicator directly.
events.passage: ARTICULO 6° — El Estado en todas sus jurisdicciones asegurará el acceso igualitario de los inmigrantes a las mismas condiciones de protección, amparo y derechos de los que gozan los nacionales, de acuerdo con los derechos y obligaciones correspondientes a cada categoría migratoria, en particular en lo referido a servicios sociales, bienes públicos, salud, educación, justicia, trabajo, empleo y seguridad social. (Artículo sustituido por art. 1º del Decreto Nº 366/2025 B.O. 29/5/2025. Vigencia: a partir del día de su publicación

events.what_changed: The decree restructured the appeal regime against Dirección Nacional de Migraciones decisions. It removed the recurso de alzada, routed judicial appeals directly to the federal chambers with mandatory counsel, and limited judicial review to legality, due process and reasonableness. This touches access to courts for migrants specifically, though equal protection under the general constitutional guarantees remains.
events.passage: “ARTÍCULO 89.- El recurso judicial previsto por los artículos 76 y 77 de la presente, como la consecuente intervención y decisión del órgano judicial competente para entender respecto de aquellos, se limitarán al control de legalidad, debido proceso y de razonabilidad del acto motivo de impugnación”.

answers.implementation_then_now: In 2023 the 2022 US State Department report found the judiciary generally enforced fair-trial rights despite delays. There was no migrant-specific breach pattern, so the MRD's 'Usually; Effectively Always' is kept as the starting rating. In 2025, after DNU 366, the IACHR (as reported in El Salto) said the decree removes appeal mechanisms, halves procedural deadlines and restricts access to justice previously recognised on equal terms with nationals. Human Rights Watch reported about 35% of federal judicial posts, including public defenders, vacant. Implementation is lowered to 'Usually' for 2026.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The protection answer holds, since constitutional arts. 16, 18 and 20 cover foreigners. The 'Effectively Always' end of the 2023 implementation rating looks generous, given documented due-process problems in expulsion appeals before 2023.
answers.notes: Courts later challenged DNU 366/2025. The Cámara Nacional Electoral declared it null on 2026-06-30 (press reports, not read); earlier rulings concerned citizenship or individual parties. None changes the 1 January 2026 text. The Constitution's text was not opened in this session; it has not been amended since 1994. Ley 25.871 art. 6 was amended by a DNU rather than by Congress.

Ley 27.149 Orgánica del Ministerio Público de la Defensa

events.what_changed: Before, foreigners lacking means had free legal aid in proceedings that 'may lead to' refused entry, return or expulsion. Now they must prove ('acrediten') they lack means, and aid covers only proceedings that order return or expulsion; entry-refusal proceedings are dropped. The right survives in narrower form.
events.passage: ARTICULO 86. — Los extranjeros que se encuentren en territorio nacional y acrediten carecer de medios económicos tendrán derecho a asistencia jurídica gratuita en aquellos procedimientos administrativos y judiciales que dispongan su retorno a su país de origen u ordenen su expulsión de la REPÚBLICA ARGENTINA.

events.what_changed: Border rejections now cover irregular entry detected in the act, and all decisions refusing entry can be appealed only from abroad. Together with the new art. 86, this takes entry refusals out of the free legal aid guarantee.
events.passage: Las decisiones adoptadas en virtud del rechazo del ingreso al país de todo extranjero serán recurribles exclusivamente desde el exterior, mediante petición efectuada ante las delegaciones diplomáticas de la REPÚBLICA ARGENTINA”.

answers.implementation_then_now: In 2023 the MRD rated this 'Usually'. The public defender's migrant unit (Comisión del Migrante) assisted migrants in expulsion cases; no source opened here documents the period directly. In 2025 the IACHR (via El Salto) said DNU 366 removes appeal mechanisms and halves deadlines, restricting access to justice. Chequeado reports accelerated expulsions after the decree, with a record pace in 2025. Human Rights Watch notes vacancies among public defenders. No source opened documents legal aid actually being refused, so the 2026 rating of 'Sometimes; Usually' is inferred and low-confidence.

answers.starting_answer_concern: Ley 25.871 art. 86 concerns migration proceedings, not criminal ones. For criminal proceedings the operative provision is CPPN art. 268, and in the jurisdictions where it applies, the Código Procesal Penal Federal.
answers.notes: The accusatory Código Procesal Penal Federal is being rolled out province by province. Its start in Comodoro Py was postponed past 1 January 2026 (press reports; not read), so the CPPN still applied in the CABA federal courts on that date.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been no right protections neither in 2023 nor in 2026

events.what_changed: Irregular entry used to make a person liable only to expulsion. It still does, and the decree adds immediate border rejection when entry is caught in flagrante. The sanction stays administrative; no criminal penalty was introduced.
events.passage: ARTICULO 37. — El extranjero que ingrese en la REPÚBLICA ARGENTINA por un lugar no habilitado a tal efecto o eludiendo cualquier forma de contralor migratorio será pasible de expulsión del territorio en los términos y condiciones de la presente ley. Cuando la autoridad migratoria constate, en situación de flagrancia, el ingreso irregular de un extranjero al territorio argentino, procederá a su rechazo en frontera

answers.implementation_then_now: The protection answer is 'No', so implementation is 'Does Not Apply' on both dates. For context, no criminal prosecution of migrants for irregular entry was documented in either period. Enforcement is administrative (expulsion and border rejection), and it hardened after DNU 366 according to Chequeado and the Global Detention Project.

practice_sources.title: Global Detention Project: Argentina's Migration Shift

answers.sourcing_note: Art. 37 was read in its original and amended versions. Ley 26.165 arts. 2 and 40 were read in the current text.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The starting 'No' looks wrong. The question asks about criminal sanctions, and the first coder's own note says immigration offences cannot be criminalised. Ley 25.871 has no criminal offence of irregular entry (art. 37 provides only expulsion, and the offences in arts. 116-121 target smugglers). Ley 26.165 art. 2 ('no sanción por ingreso ilegal') and art. 40 ('No se impondrán sanciones penales o administrativas al solicitante de la condición de refugiado por motivo de ingreso ilegal') protect asylum seekers expressly. On the Brazil and Chile examples, this would code 'Yes'. It is kept as 'No' per the method, since a disagreement with the first coder is not a change in the law.
answers.notes: Decreto 646/2025, which regulates Ley 26.165 and creates reception centres for asylum seekers, was reported by the IACHR but not read. It does not create criminal penalties for entry.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

provisions.instrument: Ley 27.372 de Derechos y Garantías de las Personas Víctimas de Delitos

events.what_changed: Equal access to justice in art. 6 is now qualified by migratory category. The provision decisive for this indicator, Ley 27.372 art. 5(h) (right to act as querellante), is unchanged, and it covers every 'víctima' regardless of nationality or status. So the indicator's protection does not change.
events.passage: de acuerdo con los derechos y obligaciones correspondientes a cada categoría migratoria, en particular en lo referido a servicios sociales, bienes públicos, salud, educación, justicia, trabajo, empleo y seguridad social.

answers.implementation_then_now: The US Trafficking in Persons reports are the only practice evidence and cover trafficking victims only. In 2021 (2022 report) foreign victims were identified and assisted. In 2024 (2025 report) CNR reported 1,256 victims taking part in investigations or prosecutions, and foreign victims had the same access to care as Argentines. No documented shift in migrant victims' access to criminal proceedings, so the rating is kept for both dates. Evidence on victims of other crimes and on irregular migrants is lacking.
answers.sourcing_note: The Ley 27.372 text was read, and its amendment list shows only Decreto 421/2018 and Ley 27.801 (March 2026, after the window). CPPN art. 82 (querella) was read in the consolidated text, last amended 2017. Practice evidence covers trafficking victims only.
answers.notes: Ley 27.801 (published 2026-03-09, a juvenile penal regime) modified Ley 27.372 after the window and is irrelevant to the 1 January 2026 answer.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

events.what_changed: The grounds for inadmissibility and for cancelling residence were widened, but the humanitarian waiver was kept. The decree excludes it only for serious intentional crimes against life, sexual integrity or the constitutional order. The relief route for victims under art. 23(m) and Decreto 616/2010 art. 23(m)(3) is untouched.
events.passage: Excepcionalmente, por motivos acreditados y fundados en razones humanitarias, de reunificación familiar o cuando se vieran afectados gravemente derechos de menores de edad, la DIRECCIÓN NACIONAL DE MIGRACIONES podrá admitir en el país a los extranjeros comprendidos en los impedimentos previstos en el presente artículo.

answers.implementation_then_now: The evidence is the US Trafficking in Persons reports (2022 and 2025) and covers trafficking victims only. Both report foreign victims identified and assisted, and the 2025 report says foreign victims had the same access to care as Argentines. Neither gives figures on humanitarian residence permits. The 2025 report notes cuts to assistance programmes and uneven victim identification across provinces. No documented shift on immigration relief, so 'Sometimes; Usually' is kept for both dates at low confidence.
answers.sourcing_note: Art. 23(m) was read in the original and consolidated texts, unchanged. Decreto 616/2010 art. 23(m)(3) was read, with no 2025 amendments in its list. Ley 26.364 arts. 5-6 were read in the consolidated text; Decreto 195/2024 amended only its institutional arts. 18 and 21. No data on humanitarian visas granted to victims was found.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The quoted list of trafficking and smuggling victims comes from Decreto 616/2010 art. 23(m)(3), not from the Law's art. 23(m), which only refers to 'razones humanitarias'. Ley 26.364 art. 5 (no migration sanctions for trafficking victims) supports the answer better than art. 6(j). The route covers trafficking and smuggling victims, not crime victims generally.
